name: Hammuel
overview: Hammuel was a male member of the tribe of Simeon, identified specifically as the son of Mishma. His mention in 1 Chronicles 4:26 places him within the genealogical records of the Simeonites. There are no additional notes or details about his life or deeds beyond his lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Hammuel means 'G-d [El] of Ham,' reflecting a theophoric element common in Hebrew names. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 4:26 and was not given directly by God but carries a meaning that acknowledges divine association.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Hammuel as the son of Mishma, as stated in 1 Chronicles 4:26. It is also inferred that Zaccur was his father, though this is not explicitly stated. Beyond these relationships, no further family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Hammuel's significance lies chiefly in his place within the genealogical framework of the tribe of Simeon, as preserved in 1 Chronicles 4. His mention helps to establish the lineage and tribal identity important to understanding the descendants of Simeon. While not noted for specific actions, his inclusion underscores the biblical emphasis on heritage and God's providential care over His chosen people.
